stories.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
stories.summary: CISA added two new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog based on evidence of active exploitation: CVE-2026-133968 (Project MONAI MONAI Label Path Traversal) and CVE-2026-134624 (N-able Mail Assure SSRF).
stories.fix: Organizations should apply available patches and monitor for exploitation, with FCEB agencies required to remediate high-risk KEV vulnerabilities on exposed assets promptly.

stories.title: Suspected Vietnam-Linked Hackers Target Southeast Asia in South China Sea Espionage Campaign
stories.summary: A Vietnam-sponsored hacking group dubbed WeaveLotus conducted a sustained espionage campaign (RedOps, Aug–Sep 2026) targeting Southeast Asian government, military, and legislative organizations in Thailand, the Philippines, and Indonesia to collect intelligence on South China Sea defense agreements. Initial access was achieved by exploiting web application vulnerabilities and default credentials in open-source software such as GeoServer, osTicket, and JasperReports, with persistent access established via reverse SSH tunnels and lateral movement into downstream networks.

stories.title: Hex Package Manager Warns of Potential Data Breach
stories.summary: Hex, the package manager for Elixir and Erlang, suffered a cyberattack on November 23 when attackers exploited an unauthenticated deserialization vulnerability (CVE-2026-129514, CVSS 10) in hex.pm to execute OS commands and gain remote code execution via crafted Erlang external term format requests. Between 18:16 and 18:29 UTC, the attacker sent 69 malicious requests affecting six web servers before Hex replaced all servers with patched versions at 18:30 and fully blocked the traffic with a firewall rule at 18:33.

stories.title: pCloud confirms password manager hack after suspicious login alerts
stories.summary: pCloud Pass password manager suffered a cyberattack, with users reporting unknown devices connecting to their accounts even with two-factor authentication enabled. The company confirmed the attack was contained, stating that a small number of user email addresses were exposed and automatic login notifications were sent, while emphasizing that stored passwords and encrypted data remain protected by master passwords. pCloud also warned customers to watch for phishing, noting it will never ask for master passwords or recovery words via email, phone, or chat.

stories.title: New Boston Scientific data breach exposes personal, medical info
stories.summary: Boston Scientific is notifying individuals of a data breach caused by a vishing attack that exposed cloud-based applications and hosted data between May 7 and May 1, with unauthorized access discovered on May 12 and a breach date of November 5. The incident affected 117,789 people in multiple U.S. states, exposing full names, physical addresses, Social Security Numbers, government-issued IDs, medical information, health insurance details, and dates of birth, though patient medical records, remote monitoring systems, connected medical devices, and clinical workflow applications were not compromised. The company contained the incident, investigated with outside cybersecurity experts, notified law enforcement, and recommended impacted individuals use free credit reports and consider placing fraud alerts or credit freezes, though no free credit monitoring was offered.
stories.fix: The notification recommends affected individuals use free credit reports and consider placing fraud alerts or credit freezes to mitigate potential misuse of exposed personal and medical information.

stories.title: US Air Force cloud platform reportedly hacked in latest federal breach
stories.summary: Hackers reportedly breached the US Air Force's Cloud One computing platform, an enterprise cloud system launched in 2017 that supports military operations, personnel management, logistics, and maintenance. The intrusion was discovered within the past month during a cloud platform upgrade, disrupting application migrations and software updates, and hackers exploited an unidentified software vulnerability, potentially exposing sensitive military operational and logistics information. US Cyber Command has been called in to assess the impact, but the attackers' scope, whether data was stolen, and the full extent of the breach remain unknown.

stories.title: Malwarebytes Antivirus: Get 50% off during Black Friday 2026
stories.summary: Malwarebytes' 2026 Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale offers 50% off security subscriptions for individuals, families, and small businesses, running through December 6, 2026. Individual plans include Standard, Plus, Essential, and Ultimate tiers with discounts ranging from $29.99 to $139.99 per year, while family plans protect up to 10 devices and small business plans cover 3, 10, or 20 devices. All subscription tiers include features like antivirus protection, scam and ad blocking, VPN access, identity theft protection, credit monitoring, and personal data removal, depending on the plan.

stories.title: In Other News: Tanker Cyberattacks, EU Quantum Act, New VirusTotal Capabilities
stories.summary: Cybersecurity researchers found 16,666 ChatGPT Sites created, with 12,830 accessible to the public, exposing sensitive data at 27 organizations including a Fortune 500 sales dashboard. US prosecutors charged the co-founder of RansomwareHelp with wire fraud for allegedly buying decryptors cheap and charging customers far more. The USDA confirmed a breach of its farmer payment system that could expose sensitive food safety and animal disease databases.
stories.fix: SolarWinds patched critical Serv-U vulnerabilities involving privilege escalation and arbitrary code execution, and Adobe addressed critical holes in Campaign Classic and Experience Manager allowing arbitrary code execution.

stories.title: SAP confirms security incident after suspicious GitHub activity
stories.summary: SAP confirmed a security incident after detecting suspicious activity in its IT environment, stating that attackers breached its GitHub environment, stole employee authentication tokens, and copied and modified SAP source code. The company reported no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data and said it had implemented measures to protect its customers and preserve service security. Germany's Federal Office for Information Security warned about agentic AI tools like ARTEX, CAIRN, and PentAGI that empower cyberattacks and urged organizations to focus on incident response and follow recommended security-strengthening practices.
